chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Khaysama who said:
I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to bid him farewell, so he said: 'O Khaysama!'

Deliver the greetings to those of our mawali (clients/followers) you see, and advise them with the fear of Allah the Magnificent, and that their rich ones should support their poor ones, and their strong ones their weak ones, and that their living ones should attend the funeral of their dead ones, and that they should meet up in their houses, for the meeting of some of them with others is a revival of our matter. May Allah have mercy on a servant who revives our matter.

O Khaysama! Deliver to our mawali that we will not make them needless of anything from Allah except through deeds, and that they will not attain our Wilayah except through piety (war''), and that the people most full of regret on the Day of Resurrection will be the one who ascribed justice, then opposed it to something else.

key_terms.أَمْرِنَا: Our matter (referring to the cause/authority of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What are the key social and spiritual duties of the mawali according to Imam al-Baqir (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) underscores the Shia concept of 'Wilayah' as a communal reality sustained through social solidarity (ta'awun) and personal piety (war'), rather than mere nominal affiliation. The instruction to 'revive our matter' highlights the active role of the faithful in maintaining the spiritual and social presence of the Imams, while the warning against hypocrisy serves as a critical ethical standard for the mawali. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly emphasis on the interdependence of individual righteousness and collective social responsibility in preserving the community's identity.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Ibn Muskan, from Khaysama who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> to bid him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> farewell, so he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘O Khaysama!

Deliver the greetings to the ones in ourasws Wilayah you come across, and advise them with the fear of Allahazwj the Magnificent and that their rich ones should be supporting upon their poor ones, and their strong ones upon their weak ones, and their living ones should attend the funerals of their dead ones, and they should meet up in their houses, for the meeting of some of them with others is a revival of ourasws matter (Wilayah). May Allahazwj have Mercy on a servant who revives ourasws matter.

O Khaysama! Deliver to the ones in ourasws Wilayah that weasws will not make them needless of anything from Allahazwj except with deeds, and they will never attain ourasws Wilayah except with the piety, and that the one with the most intense of regrets among the people on the Day of Judgement would be the one who ascribes the justice, then opposes it to something else’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from ibn Muskan from Khaythamah who has said the following:
“Once I went to see abu Ja’far (a.s.) to say farewell. He said, ‘O Khaythamah,

convey our greeting of peace to whoever of our followers you may see and advise them to be pious before Allah, the Most Great, that their rich ones look after their poor ones, the stronger ones look after their weaker ones, that the living attend the funeral of those who have just died, that they must meet each other in their homes; their meeting as such is life for our cause. May Allah bless the man who preserves our cause.

O Khaythamah, inform our followers that we cannot make them independent of Allah in anything without good deeds and that they will not benefit from our Divine Authority without ( al-Wari ’) refraining from worldly attractions (sins). Of the people who regret on the Day of Judgment, most intensely will be the ones who describe justice but do not practice it (explain the right belief but do not establish one).”’
